item.title: Escambia County residents prepare for likely hurricane strike
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County residents are taking precautions as emergency management officials brace for what appeared increasingly likely Wednesday to be a hurricane strike on the western Florida Panhandle. Preparation efforts include filling sandbags, securing homes, and stocking emergency supplies. County emergency management continues to monitor the…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County residents are taking precautions as emergency management officials brace for what appeared increasingly likely Wednesday to be a hurricane strike on the western Florida Panhandle.

Preparation efforts include filling sandbags, securing homes, and stocking emergency supplies. County emergency management continues to monitor the storm's track and intensity as it approaches the region.

Residents in the area are urged to finalize their preparations and review their evacuation plans if necessary.

item.content:encoded: Buoy data from the National Weather Service station off Pensacola (42039) is showing significant wave heights of 8.2 feet Thursday, according to Florida Gulf Signal. Easterly winds are gusting at 23.3 knots, with air temperatures around 81.7 degrees. The elevated seas are typical for the Gulf of Mexico during active weather patterns and may affect small craft and coastal operations. Boaters and beachgoers should monitor conditions and heed any marine advisories issued by the National Weather Service.

item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County has issued mandatory evacuation orders effective Thursday, October 8 at noon in response to Tropical Storm Isaias, according to WKRG News 5 and City of Niceville officials.

The evacuation order affects portions of Okaloosa County as the tropical system approaches Northwest Florida. Residents in evacuation zones are advised to leave the area before the noon deadline to allow time for safe departure ahead of the storm's arrival.

Okaloosa County and surrounding communities in the Panhandle are preparing for potential impacts from Isaias, including heavy rain, gusty winds, and storm surge. Residents should monitor local emergency management and National Weather Service updates for the latest forecasts and any changes to evacuation orders.

item.title: Water levels running abnormally high across Gulf Coast
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Water levels are currently elevated across the Gulf Coast, with Pensacola Bay running about a foot above expected levels and the mouth of the Mississippi River near Southwest Pass, Louisiana seeing rises of about 2 feet above normal, according to meteorologist Dr. Jeff Masters citing NOAA tide and current data. The elevated water levels could…
item.content:encoded:
Water levels are currently elevated across the Gulf Coast, with Pensacola Bay running about a foot above expected levels and the mouth of the Mississippi River near Southwest Pass, Louisiana seeing rises of about 2 feet above normal, according to meteorologist Dr. Jeff Masters citing NOAA tide and current data.

The elevated water levels could indicate ongoing storm surge effects or unusual oceanographic conditions affecting the region. Such above-normal water levels can complicate flooding risks and affect navigation and coastal operations.

NOAA's Tides & Currents database tracks real-time water level measurements across the Gulf and Atlantic coasts.

item.title: World's First Robot Artist Ai-Da Coming to Pensacola State College
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College and the Foo Foo Festival are bringing Ai-Da, billed as the world's first ultra-realistic humanoid robot artist, to Pensacola next month for a showcase of artificial intelligence and creative expression. The main event, "Synthetic Creativity: Ai-Da Unveiled," takes place Monday, Nov. 2, at the Pensacola Saenger Theatre.…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College and the Foo Foo Festival are bringing Ai-Da, billed as the world's first ultra-realistic humanoid robot artist, to Pensacola next month for a showcase of artificial intelligence and creative expression.

The main event, "Synthetic Creativity: Ai-Da Unveiled," takes place Monday, Nov. 2, at the Pensacola Saenger Theatre. Tickets are $35, and the evening will feature a live performance by the robot, a panel discussion with experts from the Florida Institute for Human & Machine Cognition, Persona AI, Tallahassee State College, and PSC. Ai-Da will create artwork live on stage while panelists discuss the opportunities, challenges, and ethical questions raised by artificial intelligence in creative fields.

Starting the same week, a free exhibition of Ai-Da's artwork will be on display at PSC's Anna Lamar Switzer Center for the Visual Arts through the rest of the week. The exhibition will showcase the robot's distinctive pieces, giving community members a chance to explore how AI is reshaping contemporary art.

According to PSC, the event is designed for audiences of all ages and will include hands-on community activities alongside expert discussions. Ticket information and updates are available at pensacolastate.edu and foofoofest.com.

item.content:encoded:
The Friends of the West Florida Public Library have postponed their annual meeting and guest speaker event because of Hurricane Isaiah, according to a news release from the organization.

The rescheduled gathering was set to include a business meeting, board elections, and a presentation by local author Duel Christian. The Friends group says it will announce a new date once it's confirmed and hopes Christian will still be available to speak at the makeup event.

Facebook and Instagram followers of the Friends of the West Florida Public Library are being asked to watch for updates on the new meeting date.

item.content:encoded:
The first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season is heading toward the Gulf Coast, with landfall expected Friday night near Pensacola, according to weather reporting on Bluesky.

Hurricane Isaias will bring an end to the warm and mostly dry conditions that have persisted through this week. The storm is expected to impact local weather significantly, with showers and cooler air moving into the area early next week as the system moves through.

Residents should begin preparations now and monitor official forecasts from the National Weather Service and National Hurricane Center for the latest track, intensity, and timing as the weekend approaches.

The watch applies to waters extending 20 nautical miles offshore from the Okaloosa-Walton line through Pensacola, as well as waters 20 to 60…
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service has issued a Hurricane Watch for coastal waters stretching from the Okaloosa-Walton County line to Pascagoula, Mississippi, according to alert information posted by the service. The watch applies to waters extending 20 nautical miles offshore from the Okaloosa-Walton line through Pensacola, as well as waters 20 to 60 nautical miles out from the Okaloosa-Walton area to Pensacola.

A Hurricane Watch means hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area, typically within 48 hours of issuance. Mariners and coastal residents in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties should monitor the latest forecast updates and prepare accordingly.

The National Weather Service continues to track the system and will issue updated watches, warnings, and forecasts as conditions develop.

item.title: PSC hosts fifth annual walk honoring slain professor Carla Williams
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will hold its fifth annual Domestic Violence Awareness & Remembrance Walk on October 22 at 4 p.m. on the track at its Pensacola campus, honoring the memory of associate professor Carla E. Williams, who was killed by domestic violence in May 2021. Williams had spent more than 24 years at PSC working in athletics, Collegiate…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will hold its fifth annual Domestic Violence Awareness & Remembrance Walk on October 22 at 4 p.m. on the track at its Pensacola campus, honoring the memory of associate professor Carla E. Williams, who was killed by domestic violence in May 2021.

Williams had spent more than 24 years at PSC working in athletics, Collegiate High, and the Mathematics and Computer Science Department. She was also a former PSC Lady Pirate basketball player. The annual walk has become a key part of how the college community memorializes her and raises awareness about domestic violence.

"Domestic violence is an ongoing issue in our society and in 2021, it really hit home for the PSC family with the loss of Coach Carla Williams," said Lynsey Listau, dean of students at Pensacola State College, according to a college press release. "To honor Carla and other victims of domestic violence, we've scheduled the fifth annual walk to raise awareness of the issue and provide information on the resources available to help victims."

The walk takes place during October, designated as Domestic Violence Awareness Month nationwide. PSC students can participate free; nonstudents pay a $10 fee. T-shirts will be available for $20 while supplies last. All proceeds benefit the Carla Williams Memorial Scholarship Fund. Registration is available at athletics.pensacolastate.edu/Carla_Williams_Walk.
